name: Pre-IPO growth equity
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Funding Late-Stage Growth
caseLead: Late-stage private equity gives investors exposure to growing companies before their shares become publicly traded, with returns driven by earnings growth and eventual exits. The opportunity persists because private companies accept an illiquidity discount in exchange for patient capital, while listing rules, industrial policy and geopolitical controls restrict both the timing of exits and the supply of institutional funding.
caseRest: An exit at a lower valuation than expected can reduce returns even when a private company's revenue continues to grow. Losses can deepen because funding rounds become less frequent, weaker companies accept punitive terms and IPO proceeds remain unavailable for several years. The estimated 15.2% annual return therefore comes with 24.0% volatility, a 48.0% worst fall and negative return skew, so reported quarterly values understate the speed of economic losses.
figNote: Each card shows the Nasdaq Composite’s calendar-year percentage change during the episode. The index is a useful measure of the public growth valuation backdrop because technology and other high-growth companies account for much of its market value.

events.title: Lehman failure closes the listing market
events.text: The financial crisis closed the US IPO market as investors reduced equity risk and funding conditions tightened. The strategy lost because prospective exits were delayed, revenue forecasts weakened and late-stage valuations were marked against sharply lower public multiples.

events.title: JOBS Act broadens access to public markets
events.text: The US JOBS Act reduced disclosure requirements for emerging growth companies and made public listings easier. Results were mixed because the policy improved the exit route, while Facebook’s weak post-IPO performance showed that private valuations could still exceed public demand.

events.title: Trade tensions reset late-stage valuations
events.text: US-China trade tensions and tighter monetary policy drove a sharp fourth-quarter decline in public growth shares. The strategy lost because investors cut peer multiples and applied larger discounts to companies exposed to Chinese demand, supply chains or cross-border regulation.

events.title: Policy support reopens the exit window
events.text: The pandemic initially stopped listings, but fiscal support and near-zero interest rates drove public growth valuations sharply higher. The strategy gained because digital businesses accelerated revenue growth and the IPO market reopened at stronger multiples later in the year.

events.title: Cheap capital drives record listings
events.text: Low interest rates and strong demand for growth shares produced a record year for US listings and venture-backed exits. The strategy gained because portfolio companies accessed public markets at high revenue multiples, converting private valuation gains into realised proceeds.

events.title: Rate rises close the IPO window
events.text: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine intensified inflation pressure as central banks began rapid rate rises and public growth shares fell. The strategy lost because the IPO window closed, funding terms tightened and private valuations followed listed peers lower with a delay.

instrument: Late-stage preferred shares, structured secondaries and convertible securities; quarterly valuation
rules: Companies require established revenue, institutional backing and a credible exit within seven years; exposure diversified by sector, funding round and expected listing year
costs: Estimated management fees, carried interest, legal costs and secondary transaction discounts deducted
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from private growth to valuation protection

legs.purpose: Captures revenue growth and listing gains
Adds downside protection and entry discounts
Provides seniority before an equity exit
Funds follow-on rounds and operating costs

entry: Investment made at least 20% below the valuation implied by listed peer multiples
size: Single-company exposure capped at 8% and each expected listing year at 25%
exit: Position realised through an IPO, secondary sale or acquisition within five to seven years
stop: New funding suspended if the listed peer basket falls 25% from its peak
marketWatch: Public growth multiples and the pace of new IPO filings are the main indicators because they determine both private valuations and access to exits. Central bank guidance, competition policy, semiconductor controls and changes to listing rules matter most when they alter funding costs or restrict cross-border capital.

favourable.heading: Public growth multiples rise
favourable.text: Rising public growth multiples favour the strategy because private funding rounds and IPO prices are set against listed peers. In 2020, strong technology equity performance lifted late-stage valuations and reopened the listing market after the initial pandemic closure.

favourable.heading: The IPO window broadens
favourable.text: A broad IPO market favours the strategy because more portfolio companies can realise gains without accepting a large liquidity discount. In 2021, record US issuance allowed venture-backed companies to complete exits at high revenue multiples.

favourable.heading: Revenue growth exceeds forecasts
favourable.text: Strong operating performance favours the strategy because companies can grow into earlier valuations even when market multiples remain stable. Pandemic-era demand for cloud software and digital commerce produced this outcome for many late-stage companies in 2020 and 2021.

adverse.heading: Public multiples contract sharply
adverse.text: Falling public multiples hurt the strategy because private companies are valued against listed peers despite less frequent reporting. In 2022, the Nasdaq Composite fell 33%, leading to down rounds and substantial valuation cuts across late-stage portfolios.

adverse.heading: The IPO window closes
adverse.text: A closed IPO market hurts the strategy because expected exits are delayed while companies continue to consume cash. After the financial crisis in 2008 and the rate shock in 2022, issuers postponed listings and relied on more expensive private funding.

adverse.heading: Funding terms become punitive
adverse.text: Tighter funding conditions hurt the strategy because new investors demand liquidation preferences, senior claims or lower valuations. During the 2023 banking stress, venture-backed companies faced reduced credit availability after Silicon Valley Bank failed.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy’s estimated peak-to-trough change in economic value during each event, using listed peer multiples, financing discounts and company revenue growth. Private marks are adjusted monthly to avoid understating losses caused by quarterly reporting.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated change in economic value over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn’s scenario engine projects public growth multiples, interest rates, funding discounts and expected IPO activity, then applies those changes to the strategy’s sector and regional exposures.
